findings.where: Article specimen: the pull quote “Whichever PPP Law I am currently working on with a client country!” (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The pull quote is set in the logo blue. The tile's own palette keeps that colour for the wordmark, links and the button. The quote can't be clicked, but in a page where blue text means a link, a large blue italic line looks like one. It also takes away what blue tells the reader, once Angélique starts adding posts whose real links share that colour.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank reader on an article page who clicks or hovers the blue quote expecting a link and gets nothing. Angélique may also copy the treatment for emphasis in later posts, so blue stops meaning a link across the blog.

findings.where: Hero: the “Get in touch” button (mailto:Mark.Moseley@MMMinfra.com), with the nav's Contact item (href #)
findings.fault: The page's one action is a bare mailto link. Mark's email address is not shown anywhere on the page, and the arrow on the button suggests it opens a page, not the visitor's mail program. A visitor who uses webmail, or whose machine has no mail program set up, clicks and either nothing happens or an unexpected app opens. The page gives them no address to copy, and the Contact item leads nowhere.
findings.who_objects: Staff at a development agency, often on locked-down work machines or webmail, who decide to contact Mark and find the one route doesn't work for them. This is the visitor the homepage exists to win.

findings.where: Nav bar: “Articles” and “Blog” side by side, and the article specimen labelled “An article page” but dated as “MMM Infra Blog No. 8”
findings.fault: The nav has two items for Mark's writing, and nothing says how they differ. The specimen makes it worse, because a page shown as an article is labelled as a blog post. A visitor can't tell which item holds what they want.
findings.who_objects: A visitor who wants to read Mark's thinking on PPP law and has to guess between two items. Angélique, adding a new post or PDF, can't tell which section it belongs in.

findings.where: Motion sketch: “Play again” (a button styled as an underlined blue link)
findings.fault: An action that replays the animation on this page wears the link's underline and colour. The house keeps that look for links that take the visitor somewhere, so it reads as navigation.
findings.who_objects: A reviewer, or Mark, checking the tile who expects “Play again” to open another page and sees the animation replay instead. It also sets the link look on a button as the house style for the rounds that build inside this tile.
